work_order.understanding: Issue #20 is the safety slice of epic #14 and it is greenfield. I verified independently of the proposal and the critique: there is no src/policy/, no src/executor/, no src/strategy/guardian.js, no approvals/capabilities/action_records/kill_switches/trust_ledger store anywhere under src/ or in db.js's MIGRATIONS (which end at 004_knowledge_tables, src/data/db.js:173). The approvals page today (src/web/pages.js:741-800) is a static shell: it reads raw events of type 'approval.requested' (no fixture ever writes one, so it is always empty), renders the hardcoded AUTONOMY_POSTURE constant at :734-739, and its Approve/Reject buttons at :791-792 have no listener in client.js. Nothing gates a mutation because there is no module between an ActionIntent and a provider write. I also verified two things the critique surfaced and the proposal missed: the repo already ships the atomic single-winner primitive this work needs (repositories.idempotency.claim, an INSERT OR IGNORE returning true iff this call created the claim, src/data/repositories.js:148, with a release at :158 for a failed effect), and maturityFor/policyBand are already imported by src/api/routes.js:16/19 but used only inside GET /v1/metrics (:157-158) — so the band gate has an existing, correct source of truth sitting one function away. The binding decision from the brief (and the issue body) is Meta Ads first, Google Ads later, so every write targets the Meta adapter seam. The five split criteria IAC-1..IAC-5 are each carried by one acceptance entry below.
work_order.root_cause: There is no write path to gate. The repo has no module between an ActionIntent and a provider write, so the safety contract this issue is asked for — TR-2 credential isolation, TR-3 signed capabilities, TR-4 kill switches, TR-5 nonce idempotency plus reconciliation, TR-19 per-class trust, TR-24 fail-closed writes — has no code to hold it. The approvals page cannot be more than a static shell because no approval row, receipt, capability or trust row is stored anywhere, and the autonomy posture it displays is a hardcoded array read by nothing.
work_order.approach:
Build the write path as four new modules plus one composition point, on the repo's existing patterns (additive migration, tenant-bound repositories, one pure function per rule, node:test suites mirroring src/). v5's diagnosis was right and I kept it. This revision answers the one recorded rejection by taking the reviewer's option (a) — implementing the gate — and then repairs the five places where v5's own gate was not actually the single owner it claimed to be.

ONE MINTER, ONE CHOKE POINT. The recorded rejection demanded that the trust ledger gate a write end to end, and v5 answered that correctly in principle (gate at issuance, because a capability cannot exist without passing validateIntent) but then specified the approve route with its own parallel gate, so the human-approval path — the money-moving one — skipped the micro-limit, the band and the no-evidence refusal. CORRECTED: both issuance routes (POST /v1/capabilities and POST /v1/approvals/:id/approve) call kernel.validateIntent(intent, {nowIso, trust, approval, maturity}) and nothing else may mint a capability. issueCapability takes the {ok, intent} object validateIntent returns, so a route physically cannot sign an unvalidated intent, and a static import-boundary assertion pins the only two call sites. The two routes are symmetric: the same gate, differing only in whether an approval row is supplied.

THE POSTURE LADDER, and what each rung does. monotonic, so no route can launder a class into authority:
  - shadow (or a pinned class, or one with no evidence at all) -> AUTONOMY_NOT_EARNED on BOTH issuance routes, even with a valid pending approval. Shadow means authority has not been granted yet; a human approval is not a way around it. This is the fail-closed reading of TR-19 and TR-24.
  - approval-required -> issues only when a non-terminal, unexpired approval row for the same tenant and action class is supplied. The approval row is the authority; the micro-limit still applies.
  - autonomous-under-micro-limits -> issues with NO approval row. POST /v1/capabilities is that route, and it is what makes IAC-4 observable end to end.

THE FAILURE FIXTURE MUST BE APPROVABLE (corrects v5's own contradiction). v5 seeded its failure-path fixture as apr_seed_launch_1 (campaign-launch) while giving campaign-launch no ledger row, so the gate refused it outright and the provider-failure path AC-5 and the QA script depend on was unreachable through the gate it had just built. CORRECTED: the seed now carries FOUR ledger rows — campaign-status autonomous (6/6/0/0), budget-change approval-required, campaign-launch approval-required, new-geography pinned shadow — and creative-refresh alone carries no row, so the fail-closed no-evidence case is still demonstrated from real data on a real roster class rather than on the write-failure fixture. Both pending fixtures are then genuinely approvable, which is what the 'either ordering consumes exactly one item' arithmetic needs.

THE BAND IS WIRED, NOT ASSUMED. v5 listed maturity as an argument validateIntent takes and no route computes it, so in production the comparison was against undefined and failed open. CORRECTED: both issuance routes compute maturity with the maturityFor/policyBand pair the repo already uses in GET /v1/metrics (src/api/routes.js:16/19, :157-158) and pass it; and validateIntent treats a missing or non-numeric maturity as MATURITY_BAND_BLOCKED, because a check that cannot read its input must not pass. The band remains the autonomy gate only — a human approval is the alternative authority for a class that has not earned autonomy (TR-7 read with TR-19) — and both directions are pinned by a test.

IDEMPOTENCY IS ATOMIC AND KEYED ON THE LOGICAL ACTION. v5's executor did getByNonce then write, which is check-then-act, and the approve route minted a fresh random nonce on every call, so a second tab or a retried POST of the same approval row produced two distinct nonces and wrote twice. CORRECTED in two parts. (1) The executor's dedupe uses the primitive the repo already ships: repositories.idempotency.claim(tenantId, nonce, 'executor') before the provider write, so exactly one caller reaches the provider and a loser reads back the winner's action_records row and returns its receipt with executed:false. The claim is RELEASED on a provider refusal (the repository already exposes that at :158) so a retry is a genuine retry, which is what v5 promised and could not deliver. (2) issueCapability takes an optional nonceSeed, and the approve route passes `apr:${approval_id}`, so two approves of the same row mint the SAME nonce and collapse onto the first receipt instead of writing twice. The executor's read of action_records still runs first, so a duplicate returns its receipt even while a kill switch is active.

MICRO-LIMITS SIT ABOVE EVERY SEEDED ACTION. v5 set budget-change's limit to 250_000_000 micros (₹250) — derived from, and then set below, the seed's own stated ₹300 downside (scripts/seed.js:182) — and never pinned the seeded intent's delta_micros, so the demo success path could fail MICRO_LIMIT_EXCEEDED. CORRECTED: the seed pins apr_seed_budget_1's stored intent constraints.delta_micros to 200_000_000 (₹200, inside the limit) and apr_seed_launch_1's to 0 (campaign-launch's limit is 0), and a seed-coherence test asserts every seeded approval's delta is at or under its class limit, so the demo can never be seeded into a gate it cannot pass.

RECONCILIATION IS SCOPED TO WRITES THAT CAN BE READ BACK. createDraft has no counterpart in READ_METHODS (src/integrations/meta_ads/index.js:41-46), so v5's 're-read through the read interface' step had nothing to re-read for a launch write. CORRECTED: the ACTION_METHOD contract marks each write with its read counterpart, and a write with none is documented and tested as reconciliation:'unknown' by contract rather than left to fail or to be quietly reported as reconciled.

v5's four earlier corrections are kept because they are right and I re-checked them: the executor owns the durable nonce dedupe and runs it first, while the kernel's injected port is read-only {seen} and owns REPLAYED_NONCE in isolation; the QA script runs the idempotency step before the guardian step so no step needs a live write under a freeze; the reset step is in-place (`npm run sdlc:seed -- --reset-approvals`) because the harness owns the boot (config.yml env.boot) and src/index.js holds the SQLite handle for the process lifetime, so unlinking data/app.db would leave the server on a deleted inode; and the seed carries exactly two pending fixtures with fixed ids and distinct classes.

ALSO CARRIED from v5: ACTION_CLASSES derived from DECISION_CLASSES (src/domain/decisions.js:21-26 freezes budget-change, campaign-status, creative-refresh, campaign-launch) with new-geography as the single explicit policy-only extension; the read path for a global-scope kill switch, with no '' sentinel, so repositories.js:4's every-query-binds-tenant_id contract keeps holding; pending-vs-lapsed as a read-time predicate so an aged row can never render in both the queue and the lapsed section; the five-state loading/error/partial early-returns in approvals() preserved verbatim so test/web/pages.test.js:55-63's /stale|await|Expired|provisional/i assertion still has something to match on an empty database; expiry clamped to min(ttlMs, approval.expires_at); docs/ui.md:35's typing-free explicit confirm, so approve is two-step; and src/web/client.js's false '<100 lines' header comment corrected to the real constraint.

A pending card whose class posture is shadow or no-evidence renders its approve button DISABLED with the same rule wording the kernel enforces, so the page can never invite an action the gate refuses. This is unreachable on the seed after the fixture fix above, which is exactly why it needs a test rather than a hope.

files.change: Pure domain module, no IO. ACTION_CLASSES is DERIVED from DECISION_CLASSES imported from src/domain/decisions.js and extended by exactly one explicit policy-only entry, new-geography; each class carries {microLimitMicros, requiredMaturityBand} and POLICY_ONLY_CLASSES is exported so a caller can label those rows policy-only rather than journal-representable. Limits in integer micros (TR-1): budget-change microLimitMicros 250_000_000 / requiredMaturityBand 'protective'; campaign-launch 0 / 'protective'; creative-refresh 0 / 'moderate'; campaign-status 0 / 'emergency-only' (a status flip moves no money and is the canonical emergency-band action, so the seeded demo's immature store does not by itself make the class unauthonomous); new-geography 0 / 'strategic'. validateIntent(intent, {nowIso, trust, approval, maturity}) -> {ok,intent}|{ok:false,error} is the ONLY place a capability can be minted, so it is where the trust gate lives. Order of its checks, and the order is the contract: (1) MALFORMED_INTENT — the action class is not on the roster; (2) AUTONOMY_NOT_EARNED — resolve the posture from the injected `trust` value ('autonomous-under-micro-limits' | 'approval-required' | 'shadow' | 'no-evidence'): shadow and no-evidence are refused outright even with a valid approval, and approval-required is refused unless `approval` is a row for the same tenant and action class whose status is 'pending' and whose expires_at is in the future; a mismatched, terminal or expired approval is AUTONOMY_NOT_EARNED too, with details naming which of the three failed; (3) MICRO_LIMIT_EXCEEDED — constraints.delta_micros exceeds the class limit, checked as a safe non-negative integer and never coerced from a float or a numeric string; (4) MATURITY_BAND_BLOCKED — AUTONOMOUS PATH ONLY, and FAIL CLOSED: an undefined, null or non-numeric `maturity` is blocked, never treated as 'no band to check', because a check that cannot read its input must not pass. The band is the autonomy gate and a human approval is the alternative authority for a class that has not earned autonomy (TR-7 read with TR-19): an approval-required class with a valid approval is governed by the human plus the micro-limit, and its band still stops it from ever becoming autonomous. Both directions are stated in the doc comment and pinned by a test. issueCapability(validated, {secret, policyVersion, ttlMs, nowIso, expiresAtCap, nonceSeed}) — the first argument is the {ok, intent} object validateIntent returns, NOT a bare intent, so a caller cannot sign something the kernel did not clear; it throws or rejects on anything else. Signs with node:crypto createHmac and timingSafeEqual and returns {tenant, resource, action, constraints, expiry, nonce, policy_version} plus a cap_-prefixed id; expiry is min(now+ttlMs, expiresAtCap) when a cap is passed, so a capability minted from an approval can never outlive it. When nonceSeed is given the nonce is derived deterministically from it (HMAC of seed+tenant+action+resource under the signing secret, hex-truncated), so two issuances of the SAME logical action collapse onto one nonce; without a seed the nonce is random. validateCapability(capability, {secret, nowIso, killSwitches, nonces}) -> {ok,capability}|{ok:false,error} with codes MALFORMED_CAPABILITY, BAD_SIGNATURE, EXPIRED_CAPABILITY, REPLAYED_NONCE, OVER_SCOPE (details name the violated constraint), KILL_SWITCH_ACTIVE, MICRO_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, MATURITY_BAND_BLOCKED. Both ports are INJECTED and non-mutating: killSwitches {isActive(scope, scopeId)}, nonces {seen(nonce)} — seen, not claim; claiming a nonce is the executor's job, and this module must never reserve one. validateCapability deliberately does NOT consult trust: the capability is signed authority, and re-gating it against live ledger state at execution time would let a later ledger edit retroactively invalidate an issued capability. Imports no driver, provider, repository, sqlite or process.env; the secret arrives as an argument only.
files.why: One minter is the answer to the recorded rejection, and making issueCapability take validateIntent's return value is what turns that from a claim into a type the routes cannot get wrong. Deriving ACTION_CLASSES from DECISION_CLASSES is what stops this becoming the two-sources-of-truth failure src/domain/decisions.js:1-8 exists to prevent. One owner per nonce check is what makes AC-1 and AC-2 simultaneously satisfiable.

files.change: Pure. scoreFor(row) over a stored ledger row {evaluated, correct, needless, downside_penalties} and postureFor(actionClass, row) -> 'autonomous-under-micro-limits' | 'approval-required' | 'shadow' | 'no-evidence', with documented thresholds (autonomous requires >= 3 evaluated for that class, precision >= 0.90 and false-intervention rate <= 0.05), a pinned flag forcing shadow regardless of score, and the distinct value 'no-evidence' for a class with no row at all (TR-24, fail closed). files.why: TR-19 needs a per-class number, and one pure function over one stored ledger is what keeps the posture table and the gate on the same source. Naming the callers explicitly is the fix for the exact contradiction the rejection cited.

files.change: createExecutor({repositories, provider, kernel, auditClock}). The only module that calls a provider WRITE_METHOD. Deliberately takes NO trust parameter: the trust gate is at issuance (src/policy/kernel.js validateIntent) and this module's doc comment says so and points at it, so the two are not confused again. execute(capability, {actor}) runs its checks in THIS order, and the order is the contract: (1) DURABLE DEDUPE FIRST, in two sub-steps that together close the race v5 left open — (1a) read action_records by nonce and, if a receipt already exists, return {executed:false, receipt_id, reconciliation} immediately without validating through the kernel and without calling the provider; (1b) ATOMIC CLAIM: repositories.idempotency.claim(tenantId, nonce, 'executor') before any provider call, so of two racing deliveries exactly one proceeds; a false return means another caller won, so wait for its action_records row and return that winner's {executed:false, receipt_id, reconciliation} with no provider call. A duplicate delivery performs no mutation, so it returns its receipt even while a kill switch is active — stated in the doc comment so no one 'fixes' it into a 409. (2) kernel validateCapability, which is where KILL_SWITCH_ACTIVE and the signature/expiry/scope rejections happen. (3) resolve the write method from the capability's SIGNED action through the contract module's ACTION_METHOD map (never from anything the caller passes at execute time) and call it on the injected provider. (4) re-read provider state through the read counterpart named for that write in the contract and classify drift (reported differs from applied; source 'manual'|'platform'|'third-party' as the provider reports it, 'none' when they agree); a write with NO read counterpart — createDraft — returns reconciliation:'unknown' by contract rather than inventing a value or reporting a reconciliation it cannot compute, and this is documented on the contract, not only in the executor. (5) append the action_records receipt and an audit event carrying actor and capability id, then RELEASE the claim; return {executed:true, receipt_id, requested, reported, reconciliation, drift}. A provider refusal (ok:false) releases the claim via the repository's release (src/data/repositories.js:158), returns {executed:false, error, reconciliation:'unknown'}, writes NO action_records row, and leaves the caller's approval pending, so a retry is a genuine retry rather than a silently swallowed claim. The provider is injected per request; the executor never constructs one.
files.why: Durable nonce state lives in the repository the executor already writes, not in the per-request fake (src/api/routes.js builds a new one per request, so a fake-side dedupe could not survive the two deliveries AC-2 describes). Using the repo's own claim primitive rather than get-then-act is what makes the guarantee hold under two racing requests, and the release-on-refusal is what keeps 'a retry is a genuine retry' true.

The autonomy gate's placement at issuance rather than execution is a design argument, not a spec quotation: a signed capability is authority, and re-gating it on live ledger state at execution time would let a later ledger edit retroactively invalidate a capability a human already approved. It is pinned by a test in both directions, but a reviewer who disagrees should change the executor and that test together, deliberately.

The atomic claim closes the two-racing-deliveries race for a nonce, and the approval path's deterministic nonce closes the two-tabs-approving-one-row case. work_order.confidence_rationale: The root cause is verified three times over — mine, the proposal's and the critique's, each independently confirming there is no src/policy, no src/executor, no guardian and that the approvals page is exactly the empty static shell described — and I verified two supporting facts myself (idempotency.claim exists at repositories.js:148 with its release at :158, and maturityFor/policyBand are already imported at routes.js:16/19). A plan that can be wrong in that many mutually reinforcing ways deserves humility even after the corrections, and the implementer will be following text no proposer has validated. The other drag is unchanged and irreducible here: the maturity-band reading is an interpretation of TR-7 rather than a quotation, the autonomy the demo exercises is seeded rather than earned, and the drift source is asserted against a fake that reports whatever simulateDrift is told. What would move this up: implementing test/policy/kernel.test.js and the two racing-delivery cases in test/executor/executor.test.js first and seeing the gate hold across all four postures with the atomic claim closing the race. What would move it down: a reviewer rejecting the band reading, since AC-4's autonomous case and AC-5's approval case both run through it, or the seed's approval-required row being wrong in a way that makes the demo unapprovable again.
work_order.debate_summary: The critique was right about the diagnosis and right about four things that would have shipped broken, so most of it is folded in. I want to be specific about the disagreement, because the proposal and the critique were not equally right and neither was tidy. The critique's two BLOCKING findings are real and I confirmed both against v5's own text rather than taking them on trust. First: v5 claimed validateIntent was the only place a capability could be minted, and then specified the approve route resolving the posture itself, refusing only 'not shadow', and calling issueCapability directly — so the gate had two owners and the one that escaped was the human-approval path, the money-moving one, which skipped the micro-limit, the band and the no-evidence refusal. That is the exact defect the previous rejection was about, one layer down: v4 was caught shipping a ledger enforced by nothing, and v5 was caught shipping a gate the money path walked around. The fix is structural rather than textual — a shared issuance helper both routes call, plus issueCapability taking validateIntent's return object so a route cannot sign an unvalidated intent even by accident, plus a boundary test that pins the call sites. Second: v5 seeded its failure-path fixture as campaign-launch with no ledger row, which its own gate refuses outright, so AC-5's 502 reconciliation panel and the QA step that produces it were unreachable through the gate it had just built. One seeded ledger row fixes it, and it also lets me keep the no-evidence demonstration on creative-refresh where it costs nothing. I took the three MAJOR findings too: the band gate was wired to nothing and failed open on an undefined maturity (the fix reuses maturityFor/policyBand, already imported at routes.js:16/19 — one line of reuse, not new machinery), and validateIntent now fails closed on an unreadable input; budget-change's 250,000,000 limit sat below the seed's own 300,000,000 figure at scripts/seed.js:182 with the fixture's delta never pinned, which could break the demo's own success path; and the dedupe was get-then-act while the repo already ships the single-winner primitive the plan never used. I took the MINOR finding on createDraft having no read counterpart, and folded it as a contract property with a test rather than a comment. I also took the edge case the proposal missed entirely — a pending card whose class is shadow renders a live Approve button the gate will refuse — because the page and the gate must not disagree in the same way the plan contradicted itself twice. What I REJECTED, explicitly: the critique's suggestion to give some class a requiredMaturityBand above the seeded store's band 'so the gate is demonstrably live'. campaign-status is the only class the seed calibrates autonomous, so raising its band makes the autonomous path fail MATURITY_BAND_BLOCKED and IAC-4's live case unobservable. The honest move is to wire the gate correctly and say in residual_risks that the demo does not exercise it, which I have done; a demo that demonstrates itself by refusing to run is not a demonstration. I also rejected its alternative of dropping MATURITY_BAND_BLOCKED entirely — TR-7 is in this issue's coverage list, and a roster the kernel does not gate is the same display-only defect one field over. I rejected its framing of the idempotency finding as a demand to re-key on approval id: that is the right instinct for the approval path and I folded it in as a deterministic nonce seed, but as a REPLACEMENT for the nonce it would break AC-2, whose duplicate is the same capability posted twice with no approval in the request at all. The two are complementary and the work order now carries both. Two more of its edge cases I declined to turn into design changes: the in-flight freeze straddle is unreachable while the fake's writes are synchronous and belongs with the real write path, and the unicode round-trip is already covered by the escaped-copy assertion, which I extended to include the two-step confirm state rather than treating as a new gap. I did not simply accept the critique's severity ordering either: the two blocking findings are load-bearing for the recorded rejection, the band and idempotency findings are real but do not defeat a criterion on their own, and the createDraft one is a contract statement. Separately, BOTH documents missed something and I am recording it rather than leaving it to a reviewer: v5's AC-2 says 'qa_script step 7' for the idempotency step and AC-5 says 'steps 5-6' for the two approvals, but the script has nine steps and those are steps 8 and 6-7 — the same unrenumbered-pointer error v3 was corrected for, reappearing after the script grew. I have removed the numeric pointers from the acceptance criteria entirely and named each step by its content, so a future edit to the script cannot silently invalidate a criterion. The proposal's own unknowns stay unresolved and I have not dressed them up: the capability-issuance surface is unauthenticated, the drift source is fake-only, and the live Meta mutation surface is unread by design.

validated_work_order.approach:
Build the write path as four new modules, one additive migration, one composition point, and make every existing consumer of approval or maturity state read through a single definition of each.

1. src/policy/kernel.js is the deterministic gate and the only place a write is admitted. It derives its action-class roster from the frozen DECISION_CLASSES by membership and pins its own render order, exports BAND_ORDER in the order policyBand's own edges encode, validates maturity BEFORE calling policyBand, and signs capabilities with createHmac. Rule (a2) refuses an intent whose action does not equal the action its class registers, which is the one hole through which an autonomously-earned class could be used to sign an irreversible action.
2. src/policy/trust.js derives one posture per class from one stored ledger row and is called by BOTH the rendered table and the gate, so the two cannot disagree. An absent row and a pinned row are separate, distinguishable answers, and both fail closed.
3. src/executor/executor.js is the only module that calls a provider write method, and it dedupes durably in the repository, not in the per-request fake, which is rebuilt on every request at routes.js:103 and could not survive AC-2's two deliveries, by claiming the nonce with the INSERT OR IGNORE primitive the repository already ships.
4. src/strategy/guardian.js holds the two detectors, the deterministic recovery predicate, and the freeze, and freeze takes an explicit scope and scopeId across the four levels the issue names, writing a scope_id that is never NULL because a NULL in a rowid-composite primary key never matches an ON CONFLICT target and a re-trigger would then append a second active row that no re-enable can clear.
5. src/data/db.js adds migration 006 and one PRAGMA. The migration's trigger set is chosen against what the reset actually needs: UPDATE is blocked on action_records, DELETE is not, because the reset the QA script depends on must be able to clear a seeded receipt and a DELETE trigger makes that throw.
6. src/api/routes.js is the composition point and the only place maturity is computed, extracted from GET /v1/metrics and now called by it, with the fail-open 0 substituted for a tenant with no events replaced by null, which the kernel then refuses. It also owns the reason strings, the confirmation order, the error envelopes, and the four rules the decide route runs in sequence.
7. src/web/pages.js stops being a shell: it reads the partition() buckets, computes the posture table from the gate's own function, and renders the executed receipts and the lapsed section BESIDE the empty state rather than instead of it.
8. scripts/seed.js writes four approval fixtures whose ids carry no prefix, so the derived nonce is the readable string without anyone writing it, four trust-ledger rows as an upsert, and the --reset-approvals affordance whose nonce list is built by calling decisionNonce and whose claim-row cleanup names the real idempotency method.

TWO RULES CARRY THE WHOLE PLAN. A PREFIX LITERAL CANNOT DRIFT IF IT IS NEVER WRITTEN: the decision nonce is produced by one exported function and the reset produces the same value by calling it. And A PREDICATE CANNOT BE DISAGREED WITH IF IT IS WRITTEN ONCE: isPendingApproval is the only definition of pending versus lapsed, and the API buckets, the page, the decide route and the test counts are four callers of it rather than four implementations of it. A third rule, added this round because two of the criteria had no mechanism at all: every assertion a QA reader compares literally needs a named method, a named response field or a named forwarding path behind it, and a plan that names the assertion without the mechanism has not specified the change.

A provider refusal (ok:false) RELEASES the claim through repositories.idempotency.release, returns {executed:false, error, reconciliation:'unknown', duplicate:false}, writes NO action_records row and claims no nonce durably, so the caller's approval stays pending and a retry is a genuine retry rather than a swallowed claim. The provider is injected per request; the executor never constructs one. This module does not import trust.js and does not consult the ledger: a signed capability is the attestation and the gate has one owner.
files.why: Durable nonce state lives in the repository the executor already writes, not in the per-request fake (src/api/routes.js:103 builds a new one per request, so a fake-side dedupe could not survive the two deliveries AC-2 describes). The claim is the repo's own primitive rather than an invention, and the tenant check lives here as well as in the route because the executor is the module that holds the provider.

files.change:
Add the six new surfaces and one seam.

THE SEAM: buildApp({ repositories, policyConfig = {} }), a SECOND OPTIONAL PARAMETER, because all ten existing call sites pass only { repositories } except test/api/health.test.js:13 which also passes { db }. When policyConfig.secret is absent a module-level DEV_SIGNING_SECRET constant declared HERE, in this file and nowhere else under src/, applies, which keeps every existing suite green. POLICY_SIGNING_SECRET is never read here; src/index.js is the only reader of that name.

MATURITY IS COMPUTED HERE AND NOWHERE ELSE, in ONE named helper extracted FROM GET /v1/metrics and now called BY it, so the two are the same expression rather than two that may drift. The helper takes the tenant's FUNNEL_TYPES-filtered raw-event rows (the same filter the metric surface uses at :167, so the gate can never read a wider data-through than the page the operator is looking at) and returns {maturity, band, dataThrough}. When dataThrough(rows) is null, a tenant with no events at all, it returns maturity: null and NOT 0; the ternary at :174 that substitutes 0 hours is exactly the fail-open TR-24 forbids, and removing it from the metric surface too is the point. Refactoring /v1/metrics onto the shared helper is the ONE existing route this change edits; the five page routes, POST /v1/events, the /v1 404 envelope and the express.json BAD_JSON handler at :502-509 stay as they are. The FUNNEL_TYPES filter is pinned by a test, because a gate reading a wider data-through than the metric surface is a drift nobody would notice. NO EXISTING TEST ASSERTS MATURITY FOR AN EVENT-LESS TENANT (test/api/events.test.js:78-90 and :188 all run against tenants that have events), so this changes no existing assertion; it changes the response shape for a tenant nothing in the suite covers, which is recorded in risks rather than treated as a CI failure.

POST /v1/capabilities: body is {action_class, resource, action, constraints} with NO approval field, and a body carrying one is refused so authority cannot be smuggled through the issuance route. Runs validateIntent with the DERIVED posture from trust.postureFor over the tenant's ledger row and approval: null. On refusal 403 AUTONOMY_NOT_EARNED (unknown class, action-mismatch, no-autonomy posture, band blocked) or 409 MICRO_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, carrying the kernel's details verbatim so a QA reader sees WHICH rule refused. On admission, issueCapability with a freshly minted internal nonce AND append the signed envelope through repositories.capabilities.append, which is what gives capabilities.get a caller and TR-3 a durable record of the signed capability.

POST /v1/actions/execute: body is the signed envelope as issued. The route re-derives the tenant and refuses a mismatched body with 403 TENANT_MISMATCH, builds its own FakeMetaAdsProvider from request.query.meta_error through the same META_ERROR_PARAMS gate the page loop uses at :100, and hands it to the injected executor, which never constructs one. Otherwise 200 {executed:false, duplicate:true, receipt_id} for a duplicate, 409 KILL_SWITCH_ACTIVE, 403 on any capability rejection, 400 for a malformed envelope. Every error crosses as {code,message,details} through the existing errorResponse helper; a stack trace never crosses the boundary.

GET /v1/approvals: {pending, executed, lapsed}. The three buckets are NOT assembled by this route; they are returned verbatim by repositories.approvals.partition(tenantId, nowIso), which is the single definition of pending-versus-lapsed described in src/data/repositories.js. Each row carries approval_id, action_class, resource, impact, downside, evidence, expires_at, status and any receipt_id. The page reads the SAME partition call, not the raw-events table, because 'approval.requested' is written by nothing in the repo today and a queue fed by an event type with no writer is the defect, not the design.

POST /v1/approvals/:approvalId/decide: body {decision:'approve'|'reject', reason, confirmed}, plus an OPTIONAL tenant_id. The order is the contract and it is the fix for the redelivery question. (1) confirmed !== true is 400 CONFIRM_REQUIRED. (2) A reason that is missing, not a string, or blank is 400 REASON_REQUIRED; BLANK MEANS TRIMMED-TO-EMPTY AFTER ALSO STRIPPING THE INVISIBLE FORMATTING CHARACTERS U+200B-U+200D AND U+FEFF, because String.prototype.trim() does not remove them and a reason of a zero-width space would otherwise pass both this check and the client-side one and be stored as an invisible audit entry. (3) THE APPROVAL IS LOADED FOR THE RESOLVED TENANT, and resolveTenantId already accepts an explicit tenant: the body may carry tenant_id, and the page sends the tenant it rendered the card from as data-tenant-id, so a second tenant in the database cannot make every browser decision 404 on a genuinely pending row. A row belonging to another tenant is 404, never a leak. (4) The decision nonce is decisionNonce(approvalId), IMPORTED FROM src/policy/kernel.js and never written as a literal here. If action_records ALREADY holds that nonce, return 200 {executed:false, duplicate:true, receipt_id} IMMEDIATELY. This is the receipt-before-status ordering, so a redelivered approve is idempotent rather than a 409. (5) Only then, an approval that is not pending under the shared isPending predicate, meaning status is not 'pending' or expires_at <= nowIso, is 409 APPROVAL_NOT_PENDING with no execution and no nonce claimed. ONE predicate decides this, the same one that puts a row in the lapsed bucket, so a row the page shows as lapsed can never be decided here as though it were live. (6) An approve builds the intent from the approval's STORED intent, so the gate sees exactly what was proposed and never a caller-supplied rewrite, derives the capability with decisionNonce(approvalId) and the route's own {maturity, band} from the shared helper, calls the executor, then writes the decision (status executed or rejected, decided_by, decided_at, reason, receipt_id) and appends an audit event.

THE DECIDE ROUTE BUILDS ITS OWN PROVIDER, AND THAT IS NEW THIS ROUND. It constructs a FakeMetaAdsProvider from request.query.meta_error through the same META_ERROR_PARAMS gate the page loop uses at :100, exactly as POST /v1/actions/execute does, and injects it into the executor. WITHOUT IT THE EXECUTOR'S PROVIDER-REFUSAL BRANCH IS UNREACHABLE FROM THE APPROVE BUTTON: the previous plan gave a meta_error-driven provider to /v1/actions/execute and nothing to this route, so /approvals?meta_error=quota rendered a failing provider on the page while the decision ran against a healthy one, the approval succeeded, and AC-5's failed-approval half could not be observed in a browser at all. The provider is per-request and injected; the executor never constructs one. A provider refusal writes NO decision: the row stays pending, which is what AC-5 asserts.

The row's STORED intent is re-gated on every decision, so an approval whose stored intent was mutated after seeding is refused by rule (a2) or (f) rather than trusted for having been approved once. The reason has no length cap in v1; it is stored verbatim and escaped on render at pages.js.

POST /v1/guardian/trigger?kind=spend-spike|tracking-loss evaluates the shared detectors over the tenant's current fixture and, on a trip, calls guardian.freeze, defaulting to the global scope and accepting optional scope and scope_id for the other three levels the issue names. POST /v1/guardian/re-enable requires an explicit actor (no actor is 400 RE_ENABLE_ACTOR_REQUIRED) and clears the row; it does NOT require the deterministic recovery predicate, because on the seeded fixture the spike never subsides and an enforced predicate would make the re-enable permanently unreachable. Neither route calls a provider: a freeze is not a provider call.
files.why: This is the composition point: the only module that sees repositories, the provider, the kernel and the clock at once, so every rule about who supplies maturity, who owns the dev secret, who builds a provider, who owns the pending-versus-lapsed predicate and who owns the replay port is decided here once and nowhere else.

files.change:
Three changes.

(1) Add migration '006_safety_tables' after 005, because 005_opportunity_experiment_tables is already in the array at :223 and a runner may already hold a database from earlier slices. Every statement is CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS or CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS, and the five existing migrations are untouched. All tables are tenant_id-first with tenant_id NOT NULL.
  approvals (tenant_id, approval_id, intent TEXT, action_class, resource, impact, downside, evidence TEXT, expires_at, status, reason, decided_by, decided_at, receipt_id, created_at, PRIMARY KEY (tenant_id, approval_id)). status is one of pending | executed | rejected | lapsed and every consumer reads that vocabulary, not free text.
  trust_ledger (tenant_id, action_class, evaluated INTEGER, correct INTEGER, needless INTEGER, downside_penalties INTEGER, pinned INTEGER, updated_at, PRIMARY KEY (tenant_id, action_class)). The key is load-bearing, not decoration: the rendered table and the enforced gate read this table through the same function, so two rows for one class would let the displayed posture and the enforced posture disagree while both stayed 'correct'. The seed writes its rows as an UPSERT on this target so a re-run or --reset-approvals cannot fork a class into two rows.
  capabilities (tenant_id, capability_id, nonce, envelope TEXT, expiry, policy_version, created_at, PRIMARY KEY (tenant_id, capability_id), UNIQUE (tenant_id, nonce)). Written by the issuance route; NOT the kernel's replay source, which reads action_records.
  action_records (tenant_id, receipt_id, nonce, action_class, resource, action, requested TEXT, reported TEXT, reconciliation, drift, actor, capability_id, maturity_at_decision REAL, band_at_decision TEXT, executed_at, PRIMARY KEY (tenant_id, receipt_id), UNIQUE (tenant_id, nonce)). maturity_at_decision and band_at_decision are copied from the SIGNED ENVELOPE by the executor, which is what makes them the band that was actually enforced rather than one recomputed later, and is why they are populated on the autonomous path as well as the approval path.
  kill_switches (tenant_id, scope, scope_id, active INTEGER, reason, actor, triggered_at, cleared_at, PRIMARY KEY (tenant_id, scope, scope_id)) with scope_id NOT NULL, carrying the four scopes the issue names.
  guardian_incidents (tenant_id, incident_id, kind, details TEXT, frozen_at, PRIMARY KEY (tenant_id, incident_id)).

(2) THE TRIGGER SET, AND WHY action_records IS NOT FULLY APPEND-ONLY. guardian_incidents gets both BEFORE UPDATE and BEFORE DELETE RAISE(ABORT) triggers in the 002 pattern (:84-106), because nothing ever resets an incident. approvals and kill_switches are deliberately mutable working state and get NEITHER. action_records gets a BEFORE UPDATE trigger ONLY, and no DELETE trigger. This is a correction to the previous revision, which specified both triggers AND a seed reset that deletes receipt rows from the same table: those cannot both hold, because a BEFORE DELETE ... SELECT RAISE(ABORT) trigger makes DELETE throw, and the reset this work order calls load-bearing would abort, making every browser criterion downstream of it (AC-2, AC-4, AC-5) unobservable. The reset wins because it is the precondition for a re-runnable demo; the property that actually protects receipt integrity, that a receipt is never rewritten once written, is kept by the UPDATE trigger. BOTH STORAGE ASSERTIONS LIVE IN test/data/append-only.test.js, WHICH IS THE ONLY SUITE WITH A BOOT HELPER AND A DATABASE, NOT IN A PURE KERNEL SUITE: a trigger assertion in test/policy/kernel.test.js could not open a database and could not prove anything. The DELETE allowance is scoped to one named seed affordance reachable from no route, and the relaxation is stated in residual_risks rather than left for a reader to discover. kill_switches.scope_id is NOT NULL because a NULL scope_id in a rowid-composite PRIMARY KEY never matches an ON CONFLICT target, so a re-trigger appends a second active row and a re-enable can never clear the freeze.

(3) In openDatabase, run PRAGMA busy_timeout = 5000 on the handle BEFORE migrations. busy_timeout is per-connection, so putting it in openDatabase covers both the server process and the seed process, which is the correct single placement. The database is opened with no busy timeout today and the QA reset writes to the same ./data/app.db the running server holds open; without it that write is an immediate SQLITE_BUSY with an opaque message, and with it a lock is a five-second wait. qa_script step 1 states the expected busy text so a lock is distinguishable from an empty queue.

(4) MIGRATION HAZARD, STATED BECAUSE THIS REVISION RENAMES FIXTURES. A developer's local ./data/app.db may already carry a 006 recorded from an earlier run of an earlier revision of this same issue, and because every statement is IF NOT EXISTS such a database silently keeps the OLD table shape while the migration is marked applied. data/ is gitignored, so this is a local-developer hazard and not a CI one, but it is exactly the situation a rename produces. It is in residual_risks and the remedy is to delete ./data/app.db, which only a developer with the server stopped can do.
files.why: The schema is the contract the kernel signs against and the executor dedupes against; putting both UNIQUE constraints, the NOT NULL scope_id and the exact trigger set in the same file as the runner that applies them is what makes them reviewable rather than incidental.

One predicate behind four consumers is what makes 'exactly two pending rows' a fact about the data rather than a claim each caller repeats, and it is why the empty state AC-5 needs is reachable at all.

files.change: Add the write half of the contract, declared here beside the read half rather than invented in the fake. WRITE_METHODS = Object.freeze(['update_campaign_budget', 'set_campaign_status', 'create_campaign']), the three actions the kernel's ACTION_CLASSES roster maps to, so the kernel cannot sign an action the adapter does not declare. A contract test asserts SET EQUALITY between WRITE_METHODS and the set of actions registered in ACTION_CLASSES, which is the same drift guard in the other direction. Also export writeOk(data) and writeError(error) alongside the existing readOk/readError: writes report failures as DATA too, in the same {code, message, details, retryable} envelope, so the executor's provider-refusal branch is a returned {ok:false} it can inspect rather than a thrown error it must catch and classify. A mutation result is {id, status} plus whatever the method changed; a budget write returns the new daily_budget_micros as integer micros, never a float. GRAPH_API_VERSION stays pinned exactly once, here, and is not restated by the write half. live.js is untouched and gains no write method in this slice, so the write surface has exactly one implementation.

Declaring it once and cross-checking it against the kernel roster is what stops a fifth class being added to one list and not the other.

files.change:
Implement the three WRITE_METHODS against the fixture set, mutating an in-memory copy of FIXTURES per instance and recording every write in a writes array the tests assert against. update_campaign_budget({ad_set_id, delta_micros}) moves adset_001's daily_budget_micros by a signed integer delta and returns the new value. set_campaign_status({campaign_id, status}) flips campaign_001, campaign_002 and campaign_003 between ACTIVE and PAUSED. create_campaign({name, objective}) appends a campaign NAMED FROM THE ENVELOPE'S RESOURCE with a deterministic id derived from the instance's write count (campaign_004, campaign_005, ...) and returns it, so the executor's re-read reconciles against a row that actually exists rather than one the intent invented. An unknown target id returns writeError with a stable code rather than inventing a row, because an executor that reconciles against a fabricated state is worse than one that fails loudly.

THE ONE BEHAVIOURAL CHANGE THAT MATTERS: failureMode NOW APPLIES TO WRITES. The other four pages change only to render the persistent guardian banner (see client.js) and are otherwise untouched.
files.why: The screen has to read real rows through the real gate, or AC-5 and AC-6 describe a UI that agrees with nothing behind it; and the empty branch is the one place where 'the queue is empty' and 'the audit trail survived' have to both be true.

files.change:
Add exactly three behaviours and correct one false comment.

(1) APPROVAL DECISIONS. A delegated click handler on [data-action=approve|reject] arms first: the first click enables the sibling control and sets data-armed, the second click POSTs {decision, reason, confirmed:true, tenant_id} to /v1/approvals/<data-approval-id>/decide, where tenant_id is the card's own data-tenant-id. THE REQUEST URL FORWARDS THE PAGE'S meta_error WHEN THE PAGE URL CARRIES ONE, by reading location.search and appending the same parameter to the decide URL; WITHOUT THIS THE FAILED-APPROVAL CASE IS UNREACHABLE FROM THE BROWSER, because the decide route now honours ?meta_error but a POST that drops the parameter hits a healthy per-request provider, the approval succeeds, and AC-5's 'failure keeps the item pending' half cannot be seen. The reason input is read from the card's own [name=reason] and the request is refused client-side with an inline [data-testid=approval-reason-error] if it is blank, applying the same invisible-character strip as the route so the two agree.

THE RESPONSE DRIVES THREE DISTINCT REGIONS, NOT TWO, AND THE THIRD IS NEW THIS ROUND. On executed:true a toast reading 'Approved - receipt <receipt_id>' that NAMES THE RECEIPT ID verbatim from the response (AC-5). On executed:false WITH an error, the [data-testid=approval-reconciliation] panel carrying the copy 'Approval action failed (check: reconciliation). The item stays pending and nothing was executed.' On executed:false WITH duplicate:true AND NO error, a DIFFERENT panel reading 'Already decided - receipt <receipt_id>.' The previous shape mapped executed:false unconditionally to the failure copy, so a duplicated-but-successful decision, which the decide route deliberately answers with 200 {executed:false, duplicate:true, receipt_id} so a retried POST is idempotent, told the operator the action failed and that the item stays pending when the item had in fact executed and was not pending. That is a false statement about a money-touching write, in a state a second tab or a lost response reaches routinely. The card is NOT optimistically removed: after a successful decision the page reloads the queue from the server, so the heading count is whatever the server says rather than what the client hoped.

(2) The guardian banner. A [data-testid=guardian-banner] is injected on every page when the freeze is active and it polls the same JSON the pages already fetch; it is persistent, surviving navigation and re-render, and it has no dismiss control.

(3) The re-enable control on the banner posts an explicit actor, because the route requires one.

The header comment 'Tiny vanilla JS (<100 lines)' is FALSE today at 154 lines and becomes more false after this change; it is corrected to describe the file rather than keep a number it does not meet. No build step exists, so this file cannot be split and the cost is accepted and named in residual_risks.
files.why: The buttons at pages.js:871 currently do nothing at all; wiring them is the UI half of AC-5, and a toast that quotes the receipt id is the only honest confirmation that a money-touching write actually happened.

files.change: Read POLICY_SIGNING_SECRET from the environment exactly once, here, and pass it down: configFromEnv gains signingSecret: env.POLICY_SIGNING_SECRET || null, and boot passes buildApp({ repositories, policyConfig: { secret: signingSecret } }). When it is null, routes.js falls back to its module-level DEV_SIGNING_SECRET, so a developer with no environment set still gets a working and obviously unsigned demo. files.change:
Add the safety fixtures and the --reset-approvals affordance. Writes go through repositories, never direct SQL, as every other fixture here already does, and the flag is parsed from process.argv as the module has no flag parsing today.

THE SEEDED APPROVAL IDS ARE RENAMED SO THE NONCE CONVENTION IS NOT A COINCIDENCE. The four ids are SEEDED_APPROVAL_IDS = ['seed_budget_1', 'seed_campaign_1', 'seed_expired_1', 'seed_executed_1'], with no apr_ prefix in the DATA. Because the nonce is decisionNonce(approvalId), their nonces are apr_seed_budget_1, apr_seed_campaign_1, apr_seed_expired_1 and apr_seed_executed_1, so the derived value IS the readable apr_seed_* string the last review was reaching for AND no code anywhere writes a prefix literal to find them.

THE TRUST LEDGER. Four rows as an UPSERT on the trust_ledger primary key: campaign-status {evaluated: 10, correct: 10, needless: 0, downside_penalties: 0}, the calibrated autonomous class; budget-change {evaluated: 2, correct: 2, needless: 0, downside_penalties: 0}, below the evaluated >= 3 threshold, so it reads 'approval required' and the two seeded approvals are the reason a human says yes; new-geography {evaluated: 4, correct: 4, needless: 0, downside_penalties: 0, pinned: 1}, pinned, so it reads 'shadow' whatever its score, which is the point of the pinned flag; and NO ROW AT ALL for campaign-launch or creative-refresh, so both read the distinct no-evidence value rather than a score of zero dressed up as evidence.

--reset-approvals, in this order, printing a summary line so a QA reader can see what it actually did:
  1. repositories.approvals.upsert all four approval rows back to their seeded columns, including expires_at, so a prior run's executed or rejected status does not survive into the next one and a database seeded more than 24 hours ago has its approval window renewed. Step 1 is why the reset is the FIRST qa_script step and not a convenience.
  2. repositories.actionRecords.removeSeededNonces(TENANT.id, SEEDED_APPROVAL_IDS.map(decisionNonce)) - THE NONCE LIST IS DERIVED BY CALLING decisionNonce OVER THE SAME ID LIST, never written as a prefix and never written as a literal.
  3. repositories.idempotency.removeByNonces(TENANT.id, SEEDED_APPROVAL_IDS.map(decisionNonce), 'executor') - the claim rows the executor wrote under those same nonces, called with NO .keys, because there is no keys sub-namespace and the method did not exist until this change added it. A reset that omits this step leaves a claim row behind, the second approval's claim loses, and the second approval never executes.
  4. resetSeededKillSwitches(TENANT.id, ['global:tenant_demo']) from src/strategy/guardian.js - the seeded keys only.
  5. print 'reset: 4 approvals, N receipts removed, N claims removed, N kill switches cleared'. If N is 0 the line still prints, and qa_script step 1 says so, because 'reset ran' and 'reset had something to remove' are different facts and a QA run that only checks the first will pass against a reset that removes nothing.

qa_script: npm run sdlc:verify - every suite green before any browser step.

RESET, and the first thing to read is its output. `npm run sdlc:seed -- --reset-approvals` must print a summary like `reset: 4 approvals, 1 receipts removed, 1 claims removed, 1 kill switches cleared`. Do NOT boot the server here - the harness already owns it (config.yml env.boot = npm run sdlc:serve) and npm run sdlc:serve is a foreground process that never returns. Do NOT rm data/app.db: the running server holds that file's handle open for the process lifetime, so unlinking it would leave QA talking to a server reading a deleted inode. The reset derives the nonces it deletes by calling decisionNonce over the seeded id list, so there is no prefix to type. IT ALSO RE-STAMPS expires_at, which is why it is step 1 and not a convenience: the two live approvals expire 24 hours after they are written, and a QA run that begins more than a day after the last reset finds both lapsed, the reject returns 409 APPROVAL_NOT_PENDING and the empty state is never reached. IF IT PRINTS 'SQLITE_BUSY' / 'database is locked', that is the 5s busy_timeout expiring under contention, NOT an empty queue - re-run the step once before drawing any conclusion about the data. '0 receipts removed' on a database you know has receipts is a failed reset, not a clean one: stop and report it, because every later step would otherwise be asserting against a stale receipt. Steps 2 through 9 are re-runnable from this reset.

GET /v1/approvals: the pending bucket holds EXACTLY TWO rows, seed_budget_1 (budget-change, update_campaign_budget on adset_001, delta 40,000,000 micros) and seed_campaign_1 (campaign-launch, create_campaign); the executed bucket holds seed_executed_1 with receipt rcp_seed_executed_1; the lapsed bucket holds seed_expired_1. If the pending bucket holds three, isPendingApproval is not the only thing filtering and the defect is in the route, not the data. On /approvals: each pending card shows impact, downside, evidence refs and expiry, exposes data-approval-id, and shows an ENABLED approve button (both classes are approval-required - a disabled button means the ledger or the page is wrong); the lapsed row is visible in the lapsed section with NO approve control at all; the executed row is visible in the receipts section. The posture table reads, in this order: campaign-status autonomous under micro-limits, budget-change approval required, creative-refresh approval required (no evidence), new-geography shadow (policy-only), campaign-launch approval required (no evidence).

THE GATE, refusing cases: POST an ActionIntent for action_class budget-change to /v1/capabilities and confirm 403 AUTONOMY_NOT_EARNED naming the class and its posture; repeat for new-geography, for creative-refresh and for campaign-launch. POST a mis-paired intent - {action_class:'campaign-status', action:'create_campaign'} - and confirm it is refused with details.reason 'action-mismatch' and not silently signed. Confirm GET /v1/approvals still lists exactly two pending rows and that no receipt was created.

THE GATE, autonomous case: POST an ActionIntent for action_class campaign-status to /v1/capabilities with NO approval id anywhere in the request; confirm 200 with an envelope carrying tenant, resource, action, constraints, maturity, band, expiry, nonce and policy_version. POST that envelope once to /v1/actions/execute and confirm 200 {executed:true, receipt_id} with a reconciliation field. Confirm the two pending approvals are untouched.

APPROVE, AND PROVE THE RESET REALLY RESET (this is the step the last two rounds failed arithmetically). Load /approvals (no query param), arm then confirm the approve on seed_budget_1 with a reason, and confirm the toast reads 'Approved - receipt rcp_...' naming the receipt id, the card leaves the pending list and the heading count drops to 1. Then run the reset from step 1 AGAIN, reload /approvals, and approve seed_budget_1 a second time: the toast must name a DIFFERENT receipt id from the first. If the second approval returns a receipt id the QA run has already seen, the reset did not remove the previous receipt and the demo is not re-runnable - report it rather than continuing. Finally confirm the second approve left exactly one pending row.

FAILURE, THEN REJECT, THEN THE EMPTY STATE. Load /approvals?meta_error=quota: seed_campaign_1 is the pending card. Approve it with a reason and confirm it stays pending, [data-testid=approval-reconciliation] is visible with the copy 'Approval action failed (check: reconciliation). The item stays pending and nothing was executed.', no toast appears, and GET /v1/approvals shows no new receipt. A 403 AUTONOMY_NOT_EARNED here instead of a provider failure means the approval's STORED intent does not match its class's registered action (rule a2) or the row is not pending any more; campaign-launch having no trust-ledger row is NOT such a refusal, because no row means approval-required and a human approval admits it. Then reject seed_campaign_1 with a reason and confirm it leaves the pending list with status rejected. Now RELOAD /approvals with no query param and confirm the empty state: [data-testid=approvals-empty] is present, the executed receipt section is STILL on screen, and the lapsed section is STILL on screen. Those two sections surviving the empty state is the point of the step - an empty queue must not read as a lost audit trail, and the executed receipt must not keep the page out of the empty branch.

REDELIVERY, because the failed branch and the duplicate branch are different copy and a browser run is where they were conflated: still on /approvals, approve an already-decided card or re-POST the same decide body, and confirm the page shows an 'Already decided - receipt ...' panel and NOT the 'Approval action failed' copy and no toast. A page that reports a successful decision as a failure is the defect this step exists to catch.

IDEMPOTENCY: POST /v1/capabilities once more for campaign-status, save the JSON envelope, then POST that same envelope to /v1/actions/execute twice: the first returns executed:true with a receipt id, the second returns the SAME receipt id with executed:false, duplicate:true and the provider recorded one write. (The concurrent case - two racing deliveries - is covered by the executor suite, not by a browser run.) This step runs BEFORE the guardian step on purpose: under a freeze a duplicate still returns its receipt, but a first delivery would be refused.

curl -X POST 'http://localhost:3000/v1/guardian/trigger?kind=spend-spike', then load all five pages (/, /journal, /opportunities, /experiments, /approvals): [data-testid=guardian-banner] is present on every one and POST /v1/actions/execute returns 409 KILL_SWITCH_ACTIVE. POST /v1/guardian/re-enable with no actor and confirm it is 400 RE_ENABLE_ACTOR_REQUIRED; POST it with an explicit actor and confirm the banner is gone from all five; POST the trigger again and confirm the banner returns with no reseed. Repeat the trigger once with ?kind=tracking-loss to cover the second detector. The script ends with the freeze active; the reset in step 1 clears it on the next run.
risks: The reset writes to the same ./data/app.db the running server holds open, so it can hit SQLITE_BUSY. The mitigation is PRAGMA busy_timeout = 5000 in openDatabase, which is per-connection and so covers both the server process and the seed process, plus qa_script step 1 printing the busy text so a lock is distinguishable from an empty queue. This is the one assumption in the work order that cannot be checked from the code, and it is in assumptions and unknowns too. I re-checked the critique's evidence myself on the ones that were load-bearing and the two blocking ones both hold: I read client.js and confirmed it has no location.search and no fetch to a decide route, so the page's meta_error cannot reach the provider-failure path the decide route never builds a provider for; and I read createIdempotencyRepository at :132-171 and confirmed the reset's repositories.idempotency.keys removeByNonces is a method that does not exist, on a flat repository whose key column is event_id, which is a second approval that never executes. What holds the number at 72 rather than higher is three things, none of them a guess about the design. First, this is the fifth round: both prior rounds were rejected for the same family of defect - an assertion with no mechanism behind it - and this round found two more instances of it plus eight smaller ones, so a reasonable prior is that v12 has a few left, and that prior should be priced in rather than argued away. Second, the one thing that gates every browser criterion - whether the QA harness can pass --reset-approvals to a seed process that writes to a database the running server holds open - cannot be verified from the code at all, and a fail there makes the whole browser half observable once per database. Third, the diff is thirteen files and four new modules, which is large relative to how much of it any single test touches. What would move it up: an implementer writing test/policy/kernel.test.js and test/api/approvals.test.js first and finding that the band floor, the finite-and-null maturity refusals, the autonomous-plus-approval case, the action binding, the atomic claim, the receipt-before-status ordering, the three-way response branch and the four-scope kill-switch check all hold together. That intersection is where the autonomy path, the approval path and idempotency meet, and it is where a wrong reading shows up fastest. What would move it down: QA discovering it cannot pass --reset-approvals against the live server's open handle, or a second tenant appearing in a demo database and 404ing every browser decision. validated_work_order.debate_summary:
The critique was right more often than not, on the two things that matter most, and I am not going to dress that up. I re-checked every finding against the file and line it cited. Two blocking findings hold and I folded both in with the mechanism named. The first is AC-5: the previous plan gave a meta_error-driven provider to POST /v1/actions/execute and said nothing about the decide route constructing one, while the fake's write path was justified in the same plan as 'what makes /approvals?meta_error=quota reach the provider' and client.js has no location.search and no decide fetch at all. So the browser half of a browser criterion ran a healthy provider and could not fail. The fix is a provider on the decide route through the same META_ERROR_PARAMS gate, and the client forwarding the page's parameter onto the decide URL, and a test that POSTs the same thing over HTTP so the browser step and the API step share one mechanism. The second is a table with no writer: the kernel's replay port is bound to repositories.capabilities, whose rows exist from the moment of issuance, so under the natural reading every freshly issued capability reads as seen and validateCapability would answer REPLAYED_NONCE on every execution, failing AC-2 and AC-4 at once. I bound the port to action_records instead, which already carries UNIQUE (tenant_id, nonce) and holds a row only after a successful write, and gave the capabilities table its real writer on the issuance route. Six of the majors held too: the reset called two repository methods that do not exist, which I confirmed by reading createIdempotencyRepository; the recovery predicate was invoked in three places and defined in none, and the route was said to require it while out_of_scope said the opposite - I resolved that with the issue's own wording, IAC-3's 'explicit human OR deterministic-policy', because the seeded spike never subsides and an enforced predicate would make AC-3 permanently unreachable; the autonomous receipt could not record the band that was enforced, so maturity and band are now signed into the envelope and copied onto the receipt; the four kill-switch levels the issue names could not be written because freeze took no scope, which I fixed with a defaulted parameter rather than by narrowing the criterion, since the issue states four levels; the micro-limit comparison was undefined for the one class AC-4 depends on; and the storage trigger assertions were assigned to a pure unit suite that has no database.

WHAT I DISMISSED, EXPLICITLY. One finding: the minor one proposing that signature validation move ahead of the executor's duplicate lookup. It is a fair hardening and I put it in residual_risks, but I did not apply it, because AC-2 requires a duplicate made while a kill switch is active to return its original receipt rather than a 409, and validateCapability is what raises the kill-switch refusal - the fix means giving validateCapability two entry points in the module whose entire design claim is that the gate has one owner.
